key_insight: CMC-Seg combined Mamba and CNN features to achieve the highest mean Dice (81.20%) and lowest inference GFLOPs (381.49) among evaluated models.
clinical_relevance: Automated segmentation of pre- and post-treatment gliomas, including resection cavities, could support imaging assessment, but clinical utility remains unproven.
method: A coarse model identified tumor-centered patches from preprocessed multiparametric MRI.
CMC-Seg refined segmentation using a cross-attention-guided Mamba-CNN architecture.
Ablations assessed multi-direction scanning and cross-attention.
evidence_signal: On BraTS 2025 test data, CMC-Seg achieved 77.09% NETC Dice, 78.63% resection-cavity Dice, and 4.39 mm HD95, with performance comparable to CNN/Mamba baselines and significantly better than Transformer baselines (P < 0.05).
watch_item: The abstract does not report external validation or clinical workflow testing, so real-world generalizability and practical efficiency remain uncertain.
paper_title: A Cascaded Framework with a Cross-Attention-Guided Mamba-CNN Model for Pre- and Post-Treatment Glioma Segmentation
